claims.title: Zero residue iff readout-kernel membership
claims.statement: residue readout actual comparison x = 0 ↔ actual x - comparison x ∈ readout.ker

source_refs.excerpt: Consequently, for every x∈XFadm, DetF​ρFx;Φ,Φ0=0 ⇔ ρFx;Φ,Φ0=0 ⇔ Φ−Φ0x∈kerrF.

assumptions: X, Y, and R are k-modules
The stated linear maps are supplied
claims.countercase: BRIDGE-L05 shows that this kernel membership alone need not establish equality in Y.
claims.authority_ceiling: A compiling bounded linear realization of the displayed endpoint algebra; not a result about all BRIDGE instances.
claims.residual: No quotient construction or measurement-uncertainty policy is formalized.
claims.reopening: Formalize quotient-level observable equality and any declared measurement model separately.

claims.title: Zero residue yields equality of readout values
claims.statement: residue readout actual comparison x = 0 → readout (actual x) = readout (comparison x)

source_refs.excerpt: A zero exact residue therefore establishes equality of the two observable classes.

assumptions: X, Y, and R are k-modules
The stated linear maps are supplied
claims.countercase: The theorem concludes readout equality only; BRIDGE-L05 refutes unqualified equality of underlying states.
claims.authority_ceiling: Derived linear-algebra consequence of the formal residue definition, not an interpretation or binding license.
claims.residual: The source's quotient-class presentation is represented here by equal readout values.
claims.reopening: Add an explicit quotient-space equivalence if that presentation needs audit coverage.

claims.title: Uniform equality iff the admitted-difference kernel is trivial
claims.statement: (∀ x ∈ admitted, residue readout actual comparison x = 0 → actual x = comparison x) ↔ (∀ y ∈ (fun x => actual x - comparison x) '' admitted, y ∈ readout.ker → y = 0)

source_refs.excerpt: Uniformly on the admitted domain, zero residue establishes Φx=Φ0x exactly when SF∩kerrF⊆{0}.

assumptions: X, Y, and R are k-modules
The admitted set and linear maps are supplied
claims.countercase: BRIDGE-L05 witnesses the nontrivial-kernel side of this equivalence in a concrete instance.
claims.authority_ceiling: An exact equivalence in the supplied linear realization; it does not establish any instance's kernel condition or transfer it to geometry.
claims.residual: The stated injectivity reformulation is not separately represented.
claims.reopening: Add submodule-valued admitted differences to audit the stated intersection and injectivity forms.

claims.title: Reachable decoder iff fiber-constant answer
claims.statement: (∃ decode : Set.range interface → Q, ∀ w, decode ⟨interface w, ⟨w, rfl⟩⟩ = answer w) ↔ ∀ w w', interface w = interface w' → answer w = answer w'

source_refs.excerpt: A requested answer q:W→Q is decodable exactly when it is constant on these fibers, subject to APCI’s stated reachable-versus-total codomain boundary.

assumptions: Arbitrary source, interface, and answer types
Classical choice is used to select preimages in the reachable range
claims.countercase: If two source points share an interface value but have unequal answers, the reverse implication rules out such a reachable decoder.
claims.authority_ceiling: A theorem about the reachable range only; it makes no total-codomain decoder claim, does not import APCI authority, and overlaps a prior PAL local theorem rather than independently corroborating it.
claims.residual: No linear-sector or finite-capacity result is formalized here.
claims.reopening: Formalize a separately stated total-codomain extension criterion only if supplied as a BRIDGE target.
